text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on master after merging #4219 (quant-routing heuristic). Canary run on dedicated revealed ~18% throughput drop for INT8 workloads. CI flagged it: https://ci.internal/reports/207

ci-bot: perf-check FAILED — throughput delta -18% (int8) — job 207 — benchmark=decoder-throughput-longseq — details: https://ci.internal/job/207/report

maria: copying profiling traces and heap of logs. @jamal can you bisect when you have a sec?

jamal: started bisect, narrowed to commit 0a1b2c3 (merge commit from PR 4219: "quant-kernel-selector: prefer dequant fused path"). Local microbench shows regression reproduces when KV cache hit rate is low (<25%).

alex: quick summary of the change: selector now prefers the fused-dequant kernel to reduce memcopies in high-hit scenarios, but it seems to pick a scalar dequant fallback for small batches/low-hit that ends up launching many tiny kernels. Increased kernel launch overhead.

maria: pasting sampled profile (hotlines):
```
Top functions by wall time:
  34.2%  int8_dequant_trampoline
  18.7%  kv_cache_lookup
  12.9%  kernel_launch_overhead
   8.4%  memcpy_dequant
   6.6%  attention_forward
```
Observed memcpy_dequant called 3x more often vs previous baseline.

jamal: perf counters from the failing run: CPU cycles +22%, L1 miss rate +11.8%, branch misses +4.7%. Kernel count per inference increased from ~6 -> ~28 due to extra dequant launches.

kevin: I reproduced on p4d with redwood-1-small, seq=1024, batch=1. Selector picks `int8_dequant_trampoline` for seq<128 in current heuristic, but because kv cache locality changed it falls into fallback; end result: per-token dequant instead of block dequant.

sarah: the heuristic introduced a heuristic tie-breaker: prefer fused when expected_block_reuse > 0.6 else scalar. Looks like expected_block_reuse calc uses kv_cache_probe_stats that we recently refactored and is slightly underestimating locality in multi-gpu routing.

maria: immediate mitigation options:
- revert the selector heuristic (fast, conservative)
- add conservative thresholds (seq_len >= 128 && kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.7) before choosing fused kernel
- add adaptive hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping per-request
Which is quickest to get canary green?

jamal: opening PR with a revert first (PR 4225). I have the bisect log + minimal repro in the PR description. Will follow with a more surgical patch that adds the seq_len+kv_hit guard.

alex: +1 revert for rollout hold. We can't have an INT8 perf regression in canary. Revert buys us time to craft a safe selector change.

revert-bot: PR 4225 opened by jamal — "revert: quant-kernel-selector heuristic (PR 4219)" — awaiting reviews. Merge will trigger canary perf job.

sarah: tagging @oncall for a watch during the revert canary and requesting perf telemetry check: please monitor kv_cache_locality, kernel_count_per_infer, and average_token_latency.

kevin: quick note on quality: fused-dequant produced tiny numeric diffs that were accepted; reverting shouldn't affect model output quality, only perf.

maria: thanks all — jamal, ping when PR merges and I'll kick off the perf-check rerun and sanity evals. :thumbsup:
